passages.text: Edward Jenner tested his smallpox vaccine in 1796 by inoculating a boy named James Phipps with material taken from a cowpox lesion on the hand of a milkmaid. When Phipps was later exposed to smallpox, he did not fall ill.
Vaccination spread quickly across Europe in the early nineteenth century. Several governments made smallpox vaccination compulsory for infants within a few decades of the first trials.
The World Health Organization certified the global eradication of smallpox in 1980, after an intensified campaign that relied on surveillance and ring vaccination around every new case.
Historians still debate how much credit Jenner deserves, since farmers such as Benjamin Jesty had deliberately used cowpox to protect their families from smallpox more than twenty years earlier.
Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 when he noticed that a mould contaminating a culture plate had killed the surrounding bacteria.
